svg.title: Gesture dispatch precedence
svg.desc: The ranking rungs the dispatcher sorts matching bindings by, the two filters, the enabled() fall-through walk, and two worked examples: Escape in path edit, and a bare drag with the select tool.
svg.text: The order handleInput leaves its candidates in, best first, and where the two filters and the enabled() walk sit relative to it.
Every binding whose spec matches the input
Kind, key, modifiers, target and phase all match (matchSpec).
When the pressed affordance claims this gesture exclusively,
only bindings whose target consults the affordance stay
A binding whose views includes this view goes ahead of every
binding that does not, across all tiers (preferViewScoped).
Hotkey-held tool, then the active tool, then ambient bindings.
Specificity, four parts compared in order
target: 3 for a kind that must be selected, 2 for one kind or
affordance, 1 for a body class or predicate, 0 for none
phase: 2 when channel and phase are both named, 1 when one is
drop or paste with a MIME filter: 2, anything else 1
Within a run tied on tier and specificity, an action whose
eligible rule holds now goes ahead of one with no rule
Whatever is still tied keeps the order it was registered in;
An action whose eligible rule is false in this mode leaves the
list (filterEligible). Filtering does not reorder, so it can
Walk the list; the first action that runs wins
Each action is tried once. enabled() returning anything but true,
or an ongoing start() returning an empty handle, passes the turn to
the next candidate. Nothing left: unhandled.
Mode path-edit, a path is being edited, nothing in flight. All four actions are ambient
Spec is the specificity tuple: target, modifiers, phase, typed.
escape leads on specificity (rung 3, its phase part) and declines. exitPathEdit and
tool.resetToDefault tie through rung 3; rung 4 puts the one whose rule holds first.
Outside path edit, exitPathEdit is dropped as ineligible instead.
Bare drag on empty canvas, select tool active
Default mode, which allows creates-selection. Other ambient drag actions
Spec is the specificity tuple: target, modifiers, phase, typed.
The tier settles this one: the select tool's binding sits in the active tier. Rung 4
only orders the ambient pair below it, which is what decides when no tool binds the
In a mode without creates-selection, both areaSelect rows are dropped as ineligible
